question: Can one open-set model represent uncertain future 2D scene motion in a structured latent space that supports both coherent joint trajectory samples and near-real-time marginal density maps under sparse spatiotemporal goals?

key_findings.claim: GARFIELD separates a shared, spatiotemporally indexed motion representation from three decoders with different probabilistic roles.
key_findings.evidence: A joint encoder maps an initial image and sparse known track positions to one latent z_i,tau per scene element and time. A point-wise flow-matching decoder forces each latent to retain a decodable marginal position distribution; a frozen-encoder full diffusion/flow decoder samples all tracks jointly; and a deterministic 20x20-grid classifier outputs a marginal heatmap for one element-time pair.

key_findings.claim: On OpenVid-1M motion planning, GARFIELD produces the best reported goal-conditioned track metrics while being far faster than image-to-video baselines.
key_findings.evidence: With four sparse goals, GARFIELD reports EPE 0.020, PCK@10% 0.973, PCK@1% 0.544, FDE 0.026, and 0.4016-second latency. LTX has EPE 0.025 and 39-second latency, making the headline approximately 97x sampling speedup; Motion-I2V has EPE 0.055 and 13.216 seconds, Track2Act 0.041 and 4.10 seconds, and rerun FPT 0.029 and 0.6016 seconds. Main accuracy metrics are best-of-five samples.

key_findings.claim: The deterministic density decoder makes marginal uncertainty orders of magnitude cheaper to inspect than Monte Carlo generation.
key_findings.evidence: After the 3.0 ms encoder, one density forward takes 0.8 ms, versus 37.0 ms for one point-wise sample and 330.4 ms for one joint sample; reliable Monte Carlo densities require many such samples. The direct heatmaps have better reported discrete energy score and ground-truth NLL than sampled estimates and strong baselines, while reliability and coverage are competitive.

key_findings.claim: Localized latents and point-wise generative pretraining are necessary for the advertised combination of sampling and density access.
key_findings.evidence: Replacing z_i,tau with global or entangled representations increases held-out EPE from 0.011 to 0.479-0.509. Pretraining the encoder with the full joint decoder preserves trajectory quality but makes the density decoder poorly calibrated, while pretraining directly with grid cross-entropy harms both sampling and density quality; point-wise generative pretraining supports both downstream decoders.

key_findings.claim: Joint decoding is important when futures remain multimodal, whereas independent marginal samples suffice after constraints collapse uncertainty.
key_findings.evidence: With only two goals, the joint decoder improves EPE/FDE from 0.035/0.060 to 0.023/0.029; at sixteen goals the two are nearly tied at 0.014/0.024 versus 0.013/0.017. An autoregressive point-wise rollout is both much worse and slower (EPE 0.076, 71.416 seconds) than the joint model (0.014, 0.4016 seconds).

key_findings.claim: Entropy maps provide a useful query policy for adding sparse constraints, but the paper's comparison to an error oracle is described inconsistently.
key_findings.evidence: The density entropy is used to request ground-truth conditioning at the most uncertain element-time. The text reports that the highest-error oracle performs worse than random, yet also says entropy matches oracle-based conditioning with half the information; the plotted comparison is not numerically tabulated. Noise perturbations show the entropy policy degrades more slowly than error-based selection.

key_findings.claim: Open-set pretraining transfers to robotics without fine-tuning, but it is not competitive with modern domain-specific pedestrian predictors.
key_findings.evidence: On robot planning GARFIELD scores 0.76 on BridgeData and 0.77 on RT1, close to Track2Act's 0.77/0.75 despite no robot training. For pedestrians, zero-shot results roughly match Social-LSTM, and 8,000 total fine-tuning iterations improve performance, but modern methods are much better: on ETH, GARFIELD-FT ADE/FDE 0.84/1.44 versus PCCSNet 0.28/0.54; on SDD, 19.92/34.98 versus IDM 7.46/13.83.

key_findings.claim: The learned object-motion prior is biased toward static scenes when no future constraint is supplied.
key_findings.evidence: The qualitative constraint ablation explicitly states that with only the image and no future goals GARFIELD assumes a static scene; one goal induces motion but fails to preserve object relations, while two goals capture complex motion with remaining speed uncertainty. This is efficient for mostly static web-video tracks but is a failure boundary for spontaneous or force-driven motion.

key_findings.claim: Tracker-target and private-data concerns are partially addressed, not eliminated.
key_findings.evidence: The 20M-video model is trained from TapNext pseudo-tracks, and TapNext also evaluates several baselines. A TapNext-trained model performs similarly against CoTracker3 targets, with tracker agreement EPE 0.003 and PCK@1% 0.942. A model trained on a public Koala-36M subset has similar held-out EPE/FDE, but the paper does not rerun the complete benchmark and application suite for that checkpoint.

method.core_idea: Learn a deterministic, spatiotemporally factorized latent representation of the conditional distribution of future tracked positions, then attach one decoder for coherent joint samples and another for single-pass marginal probability maps.
method.mechanism: Training videos are annotated with up to 64 TapNext tracks over 32 future timesteps. The encoder receives a 224x224 start image, track identity/start position, time, static-camera indicator, and a curriculum of known future points that falls from 50% to 1%. A three-layer point-wise rectified-flow decoder denoises one 2D position conditioned on z_i,tau, forcing local probabilistic information into each latent. With the encoder frozen, a 522M-parameter DiT learns the joint flow over all trajectory points, and a 97M ViT classifier learns a 20x20 plus out-of-bounds categorical marginal. At inference, heatmap entropy guides optional new constraints; the joint decoder produces a mutually consistent realization after the user has refined the conditional distribution.
assumptions: A single initial RGB frame plus sparse 2D future positions contains enough information to define useful distributions over future image-plane tracks.
Off-the-shelf tracker outputs are sufficiently accurate and semantically meaningful to supervise open-set scene kinematics.
The points to track and their identities are already specified; selecting relevant scene elements is outside the core model.
Each deterministic latent z_i,tau can encode a full marginal distribution even though only one future realization is observed per training clip.
Point-wise generative supervision induces latents from which a separately trained full decoder can recover the correct joint dependencies.
A 20x20 categorical heatmap plus one out-of-bounds token is adequate for uncertainty-aware planning despite spatial quantization.
Best-of-five distance to one observed future is a fair measure of planning under multimodality.
Two-dimensional tracks capture the kinematics relevant to robotics and forecasting despite depth, occlusion, contact, camera motion, and appearance changes.
Entropy of predicted marginals is a useful acquisition score for additional human or sensor constraints.

techniques.role: Scales kinematic pretraining by converting diverse videos into sparse 2D trajectory supervision.
Assigns a separate latent to every scene element and time so marginal densities remain directly addressable.
Forces each local latent to retain a generative distribution over its associated future position.
Uses the same representation for joint generation and deterministic density decoding without letting either decoder entangle it later.
Samples all element-time points together to preserve temporal and inter-object dependence across modes.
Produces a categorical spatial marginal in one forward pass instead of Monte Carlo sampling.
Trains from abundant to 1% known future points to stabilize adherence while supporting minimal test-time conditioning.
Selects the most uncertain element-time as the next place to request an observation or goal.
Uses start position and time to associate trajectory tokens without leaking future coordinates into the decoder.
Uses continuous/discrete energy score and NLL to assess probabilistic predictions beyond best-of-N distance.

evaluations.setting: OpenVid-1M open-set motion planning with four sparse goals and five samples
evaluations.metric: EPE, PCK@10%, PCK@1%, FDE, and one-sample latency
evaluations.result: GARFIELD obtains 0.020, 0.973, 0.544, 0.026, and 0.4016 seconds, respectively, best on all quality metrics in Table 1.
evaluations.baseline: CogVideoX, LTX, Motion-I2V, Track2Act, and temporally rerun FPT

evaluations.metric: Energy score, discrete energy score, NLL, reliability, coverage, and latency
evaluations.result: The direct density decoder is best on reported energy/NLL comparisons and runs in 0.8 ms after a 3.0 ms encoder, while sampled heatmaps require one or many 37-330 ms generations.
evaluations.baseline: Monte Carlo from GARFIELD point-wise/full decoders, FPT, Motion-I2V, and video models

evaluations.setting: Latent-structure ablation on held-out training-distribution clips
evaluations.result: Localized z_i,tau reaches EPE 0.011 and FDE 0.015; global and entangled representations degrade to EPE 0.479 and 0.509.
evaluations.baseline: One global token and non-localized per-track embeddings

evaluations.setting: Point-wise versus full decoding across 2/4/16 goals
evaluations.result: Full decoding improves 2-goal EPE/FDE from 0.035/0.060 to 0.023/0.029; the gap nearly closes with 16 goals.

evaluations.setting: Robot-arm planning on BridgeData and RT1
evaluations.result: Zero-shot GARFIELD scores 0.76/0.77 versus Track2Act 0.77/0.75 and optical flow 0.32/0.38.
evaluations.baseline: Track2Act trained on robot data and a flow baseline

evaluations.setting: Pedestrian prediction on ETH/UCY and Stanford Drone
evaluations.result: Zero-shot roughly matches early Social-LSTM; fine-tuning improves substantially but remains well behind recent specialized models, e.g. SDD 19.92/34.98 versus IDM 7.46/13.83.
evaluations.baseline: Social-LSTM, Social-GAN, Trajectron++, IDM, and other domain-specific predictors

evaluations.setting: Alternative tracker target on OpenVid subset
evaluations.result: Performance against TapNext and CoTracker3 labels is nearly identical; the trackers agree at EPE 0.003 and PCK@1% 0.942.
evaluations.baseline: TapNext pseudo-ground truth versus CoTracker3 pseudo-ground truth

evaluations.metric: Point-wise/full EPE and FDE at 0/4/8/16 goals
evaluations.result: A Koala-36M-subset-trained checkpoint differs negligibly from the in-house-data model on the reported held-out subset.
evaluations.baseline: Main model trained on 20M in-house clips

evaluations.setting: Synthetic multi-ball dynamics with up to 16 balls
evaluations.result: GARFIELD ranges from 0.140 to 0.196/0.186 as interactions grow, consistently below FPT's 0.260 to 0.218.
evaluations.baseline: FPT trained on the same billiards data

evaluations.result: GARFIELD scores 0.015 versus CogVideoX 0.020, Motion-I2V 0.036, and FPT 0.123, supporting but not replacing the best-of-five main evaluation.
evaluations.baseline: Single samples from three open-set baselines

limitations: Reviewer-identified; no dedicated author limitations section is present: 'scene kinematics' means sparse 2D image-plane point tracks, not 3D state, velocity, force, contact, object permanence, or action-conditioned dynamics.
Reviewer-identified: the model assumes track queries/identities and visible start points are provided; detecting objects and deciding which scene elements matter are not solved.

Reviewer-identified: training and much evaluation use TapNext pseudo-labels, and TapNext also extracts tracks from generated video baselines, creating possible target and metric bias despite the CoTracker ablation.
Reviewer-identified: the strongest checkpoint uses an undisclosed 20M-video in-house dataset; a public-data checkpoint is tested only on a smaller held-out comparison, not the full suite.

Reviewer-identified: main planning metrics choose the best of five against one observed future, which rewards sample diversity and is not an available selection rule at deployment; single-shot evidence is only on a subset.

Reviewer-identified: baselines receive materially different conditioning—text, full goal RGB, sparse points, or interpolated tracks—so Table 1 is an application comparison rather than a controlled architecture ablation.
Reviewer-identified: no repeated training runs, confidence intervals, or statistical tests are reported for the 16-H200 training pipeline.
Reviewer-identified: marginal density calibration does not validate the full joint trajectory distribution, for which no tractable likelihood or joint calibration metric is supplied.
Reviewer-identified: the zero-goal prior often assumes static motion, and spontaneous motion or hidden forces are underexplored.
Reviewer-identified: pedestrian results substantially trail modern task-specific methods despite language describing them as competitive.
Reviewer-identified: safety-critical closed-loop planning, collision avoidance, occlusion handling, and robustness to adversarial or inconsistent goals are not evaluated.
failure_modes: With no future cue, the model can collapse to a mostly static scene and miss spontaneous agent motion or unobserved forces.
One sparse goal can induce movement while breaking inter-object relations; the qualitative study says at least two may be needed for complex interaction.
Independent samples from per-point marginals can jump between modes over time, producing physically incoherent trajectories.
The full decoder can produce self-consistent samples that are more likely under the learned density than the ground-truth future, signaling shared-model bias rather than truth calibration.
A 20x20 heatmap can blur small, fast, or boundary-crossing motion and compress all off-screen outcomes into one token.
Tracker failures, occlusions, identity switches, and camera motion can be learned as kinematics or propagated into both supervision and evaluation.
Best-of-N success may not help a planner choose the safe or correct realization when no oracle future is available.
Entropy can be high because the model is poorly calibrated rather than because information is genuinely valuable, leading to inefficient or misleading user queries.
Contradictory, noisy, or unreachable sparse goals can drive a plausible-looking but physically impossible trajectory; constraint feasibility is not certified.
Domain transfer can fail where behavior depends on 3D geometry, embodiment actions, or social rules absent from web-video point motion.
reusable_insights: Use one structured representation with separate marginal-inspection and joint-sampling decoders when applications need both fast uncertainty access and coherent realizations.
Train localized probabilistic latents with a generative point-wise objective; deterministic classification alone can quantize away information and joint training can entangle it.
Do not sample marginals independently when modes are coupled across time or entities; use a joint decoder after uncertainty exploration.
A cheap deterministic surrogate for generative marginals can make active human or sensor queries practical in an interactive loop.
Evaluate probabilistic predictions with proper scoring rules such as energy score and NLL in addition to best-of-N displacement.
Vary constraint sparsity from none to nearly complete to expose how the prior collapses and whether latent capacity extrapolates out of distribution.
Audit pseudo-label dependence with an independent annotator/tracker and human-labeled downstream datasets.
Report component latency separately: representation encoding, one marginal decode, and one joint sample answer different deployment questions.
Treat public-data reproduction as a first-class benchmark, not only a small validation check, when the main foundation dataset is private.
open_questions: Can the representation be extended from 2D tracks to uncertainty over depth, pose, velocity, contact, and object identity while retaining fast marginals?
How can relevant scene elements and track queries be selected automatically rather than supplied by a tracker or evaluator?
Can one calibrate and score the full joint trajectory distribution, not only point-wise marginals and best-of-N samples?
Does an entropy acquisition policy outperform mutual-information, expected-risk-reduction, or diversity-aware querying under real human input costs?
How robust is the model to inconsistent, noisy, adversarial, or physically unreachable constraints, and can it flag infeasibility?
Would action-conditioned or closed-loop training convert the representation into a safe robotics world model rather than an open-loop image-plane planner?
Can a smaller or shared decoder retain density quality while reducing the 510M encoder and 522M full-decoder training cost?
Do the complete OpenVid, robotics, pedestrian, calibration, and latency results reproduce with only public Koala-36M data?
How much of the reported calibration reflects tracker uncertainty and static-scene prevalence rather than real multimodal future uncertainty?
Can the density resolution adapt spatially or hierarchically to capture fine motion without a quadratic grid-cost increase?

competitive_landscape.title: What If: Understanding Motion Through Sparse Interactions
competitive_landscape.difference: The same group’s Flow Poke Transformer directly predicts GMM-like local motion distributions from sparse pokes and is fast and interpretable, but covers a specific future horizon and lacks temporally dense intermediate goals and a coherent multi-step joint trajectory sampler. GARFIELD's central advance over it is the spatiotemporal latent plus nonparametric density and full joint decoders.

competitive_landscape.title: What Happens Next? Anticipating Future Motion by Generating Point Trajectories
competitive_landscape.difference: Boduljak et al. generate dense scene-wide point-trajectory grids from a single image and demonstrate uncertainty and physical forecasting without rendering pixels. GARFIELD predicts only selected sparse elements, accepts explicit spatiotemporal goals, and adds direct marginal-density decoding, trading dense automatic coverage for speed and interactive control.

competitive_landscape.title: Motion Modes: What Could Happen Next?
competitive_landscape.difference: Motion Modes explores diverse object motion by training-free guided sampling in a pretrained image-to-video model. It retains appearance-generation cost and estimates possibilities through samples, whereas GARFIELD trains an explicit motion representation and obtains localized marginal heatmaps in one deterministic pass.

competitive_landscape.title: Track2Act: Predicting Point Tracks from Internet Videos enables Generalizable Robot Manipulation
competitive_landscape.difference: Track2Act learns goal-image-conditioned point tracks from internet video and converts them to robot actions with a residual policy trained on demonstrations. GARFIELD conditions on sparse positions rather than a complete goal image, models distributions and arbitrary sub-goals, and is zero-shot in robotics, but does not close the loop to executable actions.

competitive_landscape.title: Motion-I2V: Consistent and Controllable Image-to-Video Generation with Explicit Motion Modeling
competitive_landscape.difference: Motion-I2V predicts dense optical flow from text and sparse trajectories and then conditions a video generator, supporting controllable appearance synthesis. GARFIELD omits video rendering, models selected point tracks and their uncertainty, and supports sparse temporal goals; Motion-I2V becomes much stronger when supplied full trajectories, a denser condition than GARFIELD requires.

novelty_assessment: Author claim: GARFIELD is an open-set probabilistic kinematics representation that uniquely combines spatially and temporally sparse goals, coherent joint trajectory sampling, and constant-pass nonparametric marginal density access, yielding 97x faster motion samples than video models and two-orders-faster density estimates. Reviewer inference: direct sparse motion distributions, point-trajectory world models, goal-conditioned tracks, and diverse motion sampling all predate this paper, including the same group's FPT. The defensible novelty is the unified localized latent trained by point-wise generation and reused by both a joint full decoder and a fast categorical density decoder across time. The broader 'underlying distribution' language should be narrowed: the deterministic decoder exposes learned point-wise marginals, not a tractable joint density; full-joint calibration is not established, and the task remains supplied-query 2D tracking rather than general scene physics.
reviewer_notes: Full text, implementation, metrics, conceptual comparisons, extended evaluations, ablations, and qualitative appendix were checked through page 35. No explicit limitations section was found, so limitations labeled reviewer-identified are inferences from the protocols and results. Two reporting tensions are preserved: the entropy policy is said both to beat an error oracle that is worse than random and to match oracle conditioning with half the information; and generated samples being more likely than ground truth under the learned marginal density can indicate decoder agreement but not necessarily calibration to reality. Primary competitors were independently checked through arXiv or official CVF proceedings: 2510.12777, 2509.21592, 2412.00148, 2405.01527, and 2401.15977.
